status: Pilot, written by Claude on 12 November 2026, checked by the translation workers, and deployed to earthfluent.com on 13 November 2026. Informal du throughout.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - Two Dots Over a Vowel, Part 1
lessons.description: Two dots over a vowel change its sound, and often the word. Hear schon against schön, and Mutter against Mütter.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - The Letter ß, Part 1
lessons.description: The letter ß is a sharp s, written after a long vowel or a vowel pair like ei. Hear it in Straße, groß, heiß, and Fuß.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - Ch, Soft and Hard, Part 1
lessons.description: After i and e, ch is a soft hiss. After a, o, and u, it is made at the back of the throat. Hear ich and nicht, then Buch and Nacht.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - Naming Words Take a Capital, Part 1
lessons.description: Every naming word is written with a capital letter, wherever it stands. That is how you tell essen, to eat, from das Essen, the food.

lessons.title: Patterns - To Go in the Present, Part 1
lessons.description: The verb gehen, to go, changes its ending to say who is going. Spot what changes: gehe, gehst, geht, gehen.

lessons.title: Patterns - To Go in the Present, Part 2
lessons.description: More of gehen, to go: for all of you, for them, for "let's", and for what you are off to do.

lessons.title: Patterns - More Than One, Part 1
lessons.description: German makes more than one in several ways: an added e here, an added n there. The word for the is die for all of them.

lessons.title: Patterns - Three Words for The, Part 1
lessons.description: Every naming word is a he-word, a she-word, or an it-word, and takes der, die, or das. It is learned with the word: the girl is das Mädchen.

lessons.title: Sentence Building - Asking a Question, Part 1
lessons.description: To ask a question, the verb moves to the front of the sentence.
words: This is the bus to Berlin.
Das ist der Bus nach Berlin.
Is this the bus to Berlin?
Ist das der Bus nach Berlin?

lessons.title: Sentence Building - Saying No, Part 1
lessons.description: The word nicht says not. It comes after the verb, and often at the very end.

lessons.title: Sentence Building - The Verb Comes Second, Part 1
lessons.description: In a plain statement, the verb is always the second piece of the sentence. Start with today, and I has to move behind the verb.

lessons.title: Sentence Building - Describing Words Come First, Part 1
lessons.description: As in English, the describing word comes before the thing. Its ending changes to match the thing: weißes, schwarze, großer.

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Going Places, Part 1
lessons.description: The verb gehen, to go, at work in whole sentences, and fahren, which German uses for going on wheels.
words: I am going to the market.
We are going to the beach.
Are you going to the party?

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Questions and Answers, Part 1
lessons.description: A question and its answer, side by side. Before a thing, not becomes kein, so German says I speak no English: ich spreche kein Englisch.
words: No, I do not speak English.

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Describing Things, Part 1
lessons.description: After ist and sind, the describing word takes no ending at all: weiß, rot, groß, klein.

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Yesterday, Today, and Tomorrow, Part 1
lessons.description: One trip to the market, told three ways. Watch the verb keep its second place every time.
words: I went to the market yesterday.
Gestern bin ich zum Markt gegangen.
I am going to the market today.
I will go to the market tomorrow.
Morgen werde ich zum Markt gehen.
